requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND account_id = 30 AND contact_id = 64 AND product_id = 17 AND channel = 'email' AND priority = 'high' AND state IN ('new', 'in_progress')
requirements.source: High priority case created for Perry Watts
assumptions: Perry Watts is user 727, whose contact record 64 belongs to account 30 (Johnson, Rivera and Carr)
Atlassian Jira Data Center is product 17 (exact name; the Variant products are different products)
channel email from 'email as a communication'; priority high as stated
state: the policy gives new for a case with no group or user and in_progress once SLA tracking or work begins; the request fixes neither, so either is accepted

disagreement: state: A not tested, B IN ('new', 'in_progress'); chose B because both policy states are accepted and the tighter predicate rules out a newly registered case left pending, resolved, closed or canceled

notes:
disagreement: case state: one pass leaves it untested, the other accepts new or in_progress; chose the tighter predicate, since both policy states are accepted and a newly registered case should be in neither pending, resolved, closed nor canceled
disagreement: interaction anchor: one pass anchors interaction 1233, the other selects by case_id = 1233; chose the anchor, since the task creates exactly one interaction
disagreement: knowledge link anchor: one pass anchors case_knowledge 528, the other selects by case and article; chose the anchor, since the task creates exactly one case_knowledge row
disagreement: stay on unpublished articles: one pass guards only the draft article 26, the other every article not in state published; chose the wider guard, which covers 26 and everything else the policy forbids linking
The two SLA definition checks test only rows that already exist (2 'SLA Response - High' and 7 'SLA Resolution - High'), so they are weak. They suggest the benchmark expected the high-priority SLAs to be linked to the case, but the request only registers the case and the policy links SLAs when work on the case begins (state in_progress); no case_sla row is required, and the case state accepts new or in_progress for the same reason. Account 30 holds an active product entitlement for product 17 (278, premium).
Installed product 162 (account 30, product 17, in use) is not required on the case: the policy accepts a product or an installed product, the request names only the product, and the benchmark tests product_id only.
The case's short description is not tested: the policy's template ('Product: <name>, Issue: is not working as expected.') is a format rule the benchmark does not test.
The acting user, Karen Watkins (user 39), is an active admin, so registering the case and linking knowledge are allowed.
